audit_items.proof_trace: Cookie deletion (L113-119) is guarded by `if (!error)` inside `if (code)`, so both the code-exchange-error path (L124) and the no-code path (L128) return without emitting Set-Cookie delete headers. The `oauth_redirect` httpOnly cookie—set by `/oauth/authorize` to capture the full OAuth authorization URL—persists in the browser after any failed callback, violating the post-condition for those paths.
audit_items.attack_scenario: An attacker induces a failed auth callback (e.g., replaying an expired code) while the victim has an `oauth_redirect` cookie pointing to a malicious third-party OAuth grant flow; on the victim's next successful login the stale cookie redirects them silently into that OAuth consent, potentially granting the attacker's client unintended authorization.
